name: Comparing density using equal volumes
reuseRationale: Material Properties Vocabulary names density but does not assess relational comparison; The Particle Model requires a different microscopic explanatory model. Existing mass and volume topics measure separate quantities, not their relationship. This is a distinct conceptual claim, not an easier copy of particle theory.
scopeNotes: Age 9–12 is proposed global teaching guidance, not a certified jurisdiction mapping.
Concrete comparison can precede formal division and particle theory.

name: Water displaced by immersed objects
reuseRationale: What volume means concerns unit-cube volume, and ordinary-pouring conservation concerns unchanged liquid amount. Neither assesses the relation between immersed object volume and displaced liquid. The new claim does not duplicate measuring an irregular object by subtraction as a procedure.
scopeNotes: Middle-school displacement material supports the physics; the simpler primary activity is original authoring.
This conceptual claim does not certify the graduated-cylinder measurement procedure.

name: Buoyant support and floating
reuseRationale: Forces Vocabulary names upthrust; density vocabulary and particle explanations do not establish the relation between water displacement, support and load. This claim integrates a single flotation model and retains pressure mechanism as an optional explanation, not a required whole bundled pressure topic.
scopeNotes: Primary flotation teaching has classroom evidence, but these exact activities have not been tested.
Assessment design is included in the graph; learner efficacy testing is not a release gate for this project.

name: Pressure in still liquids
reuseRationale: Deformation & Fluid Pressure bundles this concept with elastic/inelastic deformation and thermal expansion. The new focused claim extracts independently assessable hydrostatics without changing or retiring the older broader claim or transferring its mastery. Moments, Pressure & Hooke's Law also includes independent content and cannot substitute.
scopeNotes: Proposed primary age guidance is 10–12; technical sources do not establish an exact age threshold.
Older bundled topic and research remain unchanged; overlap is documented, not silently merged.

name: Sensing and acting in physical control systems
reuseRationale: Parts of a computer classifies/selects peripherals and Real-World Robots identifies examples. Decisions and input in programs implements branching. This claim assesses the causal physical chain and power-versus-information distinction, independently of writing code.
scopeNotes: Age guidance is a proposed primary teaching range.
Physical control is a curriculum component; no full standard coverage is asserted.

name: Correcting a system using feedback
reuseRationale: Loops and input decisions implement execution structures but do not require the measured output to feed back into a regulating action. A thermostat-style causal loop is independently explainable from code construction; do not create separate rover/submarine feedback nodes.
scopeNotes: Technical feedback sources support correctness, not an experimentally established primary age threshold.
Repeated sensor use is supported by primary lesson guidance; closed-loop regulator examples are original bounded applications.

name: Force and travel in simple machines
reuseRationale: Simple machine arrangements and everyday uses assesses recognition and function. Levers, Pulleys & Gears assesses force-changing mechanisms but does not require the reciprocal input-travel explanation. Efficiency, Sankey diagrams, and work done requires numerical efficiency and diagrams. This qualitative energy/travel relationship is independently assessable; separate topic copies for each tool are unnecessary.
scopeNotes: Primary ages are proposed, not a new statutory mapping.
Year 5 mechanism recognition is related; the explicit travel/energy tradeoff extends that requirement.

name: Load placement and static tipping
reuseRationale: Balanced & Unbalanced Forces concerns investigation of net force and motion, not the support-region condition for tipping. Moments, Pressure & Hooke's Law bundles numerical torque, hydraulics and elasticity. The proposed claim is the spatial static-stability criterion, with supplied combined centre markers, not an easier replacement for the whole older claim.
scopeNotes: Related to England D&T stability practice, but conceptual prediction alone does not cover building structures.
Formal turning effects occur in England KS3; the proposed earlier qualitative model is enrichment.

name: Contact force spread over an area
reuseRationale: Deformation & Fluid Pressure covers elastic change, thermal expansion and fluid depth. Moments, Pressure & Hooke's Law covers other bundled quantitative claims. Neither assesses the controlled solid-contact force/area comparison; force vocabulary alone is insufficient.
scopeNotes: Qualitative enrichment relative to England primary Science; ratio pressure is explicit at KS3.
This is not the same claim as hydrostatic pressure with depth.

name: Solar-panel orientation and light capture
reuseRationale: Sunlight warms things up concerns thermal effects. Building an energy-converting device is a design/test procedure, and Energy stores and transfers classifies stores/pathways. None assesses geometric interception by a photovoltaic surface; successful device construction alone does not demonstrate that explanation.
scopeNotes: Application enrichment; no exact primary curriculum mapping asserted.
Technical source supports orientation effects, not a validated primary-age sequence.
